dedupe_keys.name: trek medics global database for emergency and ambulance services

description: This database profiles national emergency medical and ambulance systems country by country. It is maintained by Trek Medics International, a non-profit that builds dispatch tools for emergency services, to give one place to learn how to call for help in each country and how the systems are organised and run. Each country page assesses the system in six categories: public access (a single toll-free emergency number and rural reach), workforce (responder training and curricula), transport (vehicle types, vehicles per population, response times, safety standards and equipment), clinical emergency care at receiving hospitals, and further categories on oversight and system organisation. Coverage is about 42 countries across all continents, from Argentina and Ghana to Japan and Zimbabwe. Pages are free to read on the web; there is no bulk download and the licence is not stated. Caveats: profiles are compiled from mixed sources and contributors, update dates vary, and entries are narrative, not a consistent numeric table. Simulation uses: context and parameters, such as emergency numbers, fleet ratios and response times, for emergency medical service models in countries without open dispatch data. Related records: the Liberia national emergency medical service study (case_study-liberia-national-ems-first-22-months) describes one national system in detail.
